speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative review. Since you are experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty tolerating earrings after your tympanoplasty, I need to clarify the timeline and nature of these symptoms. How many weeks have passed since your surgery, and does the pain radiate behind your ear or to your jaw?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Recurrent Cholesteatoma. The patient's history of chronic infections, recent tympanoplasty, and specifically the "shooting pain when eating" (referred pain from the temporomandibular joint/inner ear) and pain with pressure on the ear canal (earrings) strongly suggests the failure of the graft or recurrence of the disease process.
